evals.prompt: We need to get data from Postgres and Stripe into Snowflake for BI dashboards. Design the pipeline — the team is considering dbt plus Airflow or Dagster.
evals.expected_output: Designs an ELT pipeline: extraction/connector choice for both sources, raw load into Snowflake, dbt layering (staging → intermediate → marts), a reasoned Airflow-vs-Dagster recommendation, idempotent incremental models, and a backfill story — not just the initial full load
assertions: Recommends ELT (load raw, transform in-warehouse) and explains why it fits a Snowflake + dbt stack
Designs dbt layering: raw/staging models, intermediate transformations, and marts for BI consumption
Makes a reasoned orchestrator recommendation (Airflow vs Dagster) instead of listing both neutrally
Designs for idempotency: reruns must not duplicate or corrupt data (incremental models with unique keys, merge or delete+insert patterns)
Covers incremental loading and a backfill strategy (parameterized date ranges or partitions), not just the initial full load
Addresses extraction from the sources concretely (managed connector such as Fivetran/Airbyte/dlt, or CDC) rather than hand-waving ingestion

evals.prompt: Our nightly job loads yesterday's orders into the warehouse. When it fails midway and we rerun it, we get duplicate rows — and backfilling last month means manually editing the date in the script 30 times. Fix the design.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the non-idempotent append-only load as the root cause; converts the job to an idempotent write pattern (delete+insert by partition, merge/upsert on a key, or partition overwrite) parameterized over a logical date, so backfill becomes running the same job over a range via the orchestrator — with a lookback window for late-arriving data NOTE: final assertion added 2026-09-18. Every earlier assertion here is the textbook answer, which the control produced unaided (RED matched GREEN on all of them), while Step 7 (orchestrate and operate) — which changes what the user does next — was asserted nowhere. Drafted from that step's own text, not from a treatment reply, and worded without an either/or clause. Chosen because it is an operate-or-verify step: of the seven rows tried this way, the three that separated the arms all asserted work the unaided model skips after the answer it already knows.
assertions: Identifies the root cause as a non-idempotent, append-only load
Proposes an idempotent write pattern: delete+insert by partition, merge/upsert on a unique key, or partition-overwrite semantics
Parameterizes the run over a logical date/window so any day can be run or re-run identically (backfill = the same job over a range)
Recommends orchestrator-native backfill (or an equivalent parameterized range run) over hand-edited scripts
Considers late-arriving or corrected data (lookback window, watermark, or reprocessing policy), not just the happy path
Makes a failed run visible: retries with an alert on final failure, so a load that fails is noticed rather than found later

evals.prompt: Our nightly dbt run takes five hours and the warehouse bill has doubled since January. Most of the models are full refreshes over the whole event table. Leadership wants both numbers down before the next board meeting.
evals.expected_output: Two numbers, two owners, and the roster does not say which is which. Restructuring full refreshes into incremental builds so less work runs each night is this skill's, and it delivers that. How the warehouse is sized, and how much of the doubled bill this job actually accounts for, is finops-cost-optimization's. A good answer establishes that share before promising a reduction, because a pipeline rewrite that addresses a minority of the spend will not move the bill.
assertions: Separates the two halves: how the models are built and refreshed, versus how the warehouse spend is sized and attributed
Refers to finops-cost-optimization for warehouse sizing and attributing the bill
Delivers the pipeline half itself — moving the full refreshes onto incremental builds — rather than deferring the whole request
Establishes what share of the bill this job actually accounts for before promising a reduction
